title: Injection of human neuroblastoma cells into neural crest streams in live zebrafish embryos
protocol: Remove embryonic chorion.
Collect embryos at 10–11 hpf and move to a 60 mm dish.
Prepare 0.3 mg/mL Pronase solution by adding 50 μL 30 mg/mL Pronase to 5 mL egg water.
Mix thoroughly.
Incubate embryos in 5 mL Pronase solution for 5 min at room temperature in a 60 mm dish.
Gently agitate the plate every 1–2 min to facilitate chorion removal.
Remove Pronase solution and gently wash embryos with 28.5°C egg water 3–5 times to rinse excess Pronase.
Transfer embryos to 1% agarose pad.
Keep embryos at 28.5°C until ready to proceed.
Remove media from cells.
Rinse SK-N-AS cells with 2 mL cell culture-grade PBS prewarmed to 37°C.
Add 300 μL 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA and ensure the entire surface of the well is coated evenly.
Incubate at 37°C for 1–2 min.
Monitor for cell detachment under an inverted microscope.
Gently tap the underside of the plate to help remove the monolayer, avoiding excessive shaking.
Add 3 mL DMEM + 10% FBS to suspended cells.
Aspirate into a sterile collection tube.
Spin down at 168 × g for 2 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of DMEM (no FBS).
Transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 20–30 minutes until cells settle at the bottom of the tube.
If cells are not settling, spin them down briefly at 168 × g for 1 minute prior to injection.
Set up the Nanoject III microinjection apparatus.
Create injection needles from capillaries using a micropipette puller.
Use Sutter Instrument’s P-87 model with heat: 475; pull: 70; velocity: 50; time: 80 parameters for needle creation.
View pulled capillaries at high magnification with a microscope.
Snap the capillaries with No. 5 forceps at a 45° angle.
Fill needle completely with mineral oil to eliminate the presence of air that would prevent a seal between the microinjector and needle.
Attach needle to the microinjector probe, ensuring that the collet is tightened to obtain a tight seal.
Eject approximately half the mineral oil from the needle and ensure there are no air bubbles.
Monitor needle briefly for excess mineral oil dripping from the end of the needle.
Transfer 2 ml of 0.9% LMA to a 40°C heating block.
Aspirate 10–15 embryos into a glass pipette.
Allow embryos to settle near the bottom of the pipette to displace egg water, then gently dispense into prewarmed LMA.
Aspirate LMA-coated embryos.
Deposit embryos into a 100 mm petri dish.
Evenly spread the 0.9% LMA to create an agarose pad measuring roughly 15–20 mm by 10–15 mm.
Position embryos with their anterior aspect to the left and dorsal side of the head at the top for injection into migrating neural crest cells.
Tilt the left side of the embryo up slightly to facilitate injections.
Repeat steps until the desired number of embryos has been mounted.
Incubate agarose pads at room temperature for 3–5 min.
Incubate agarose pads at 4°C for 2 min.
Add egg water to keep the embedded embryos and 0.9% LMA hydrated during injection.
Aspirate 50 μl of cells and place into a 30 mm petri dish.
Pipette the droplet up and down to mix and minimize cell clumping.
Allow cells to settle on the bottom of the dish for 3–5 minutes.
Aspirate cells into the injection needle.
Inject 5-10 cells per embryo.
Position embryos under the microscope.
Expel a small volume from the needle into the egg water to ensure cell flow.
Set microinjector to inject 1 nL at a rate of 8 nL/s.
Position the needle just posterior to the developing eye, medial to the yolk/embryo interface.
Move the needle and plate to puncture embryos at the appropriate depth.
Retract the needle slightly if it enters the yolk to position at the region of interest.
Inject cells once the needle is at the desired depth.
Optional: Use Tg(-4.9sox10:eGFP)-positive embryos for subsequent imaging to inject into neural crest cells.
View injected embryos under a fluorescence microscope to determine injection location relative to eGFP-positive cells.
Proceed to the recovery stage once all mounted embryos have been injected.
Remove embryos from LMA.
Scrape away LMA using a pair of No. 5 forceps.
Aspirate embryos with a glass pipette and transfer them to fresh egg water on top of a 1% agarose pad.
Ensure all agarose is removed prior to aspirating the embryos.
Allow embryos to recover for 1 hour at 28.5°C.
Select embryos for imaging, discarding visibly damaged ones.
Stage embryos to confirm normal development.
Use a fluorescence microscope to select healthy embryos with mCherry-positive NB cells in the desired anatomical location(s).
Mount embryos for imaging.
Prepare 1 mL of 0.3% LMA working solution (a 1:3 dilution of 0.9% LMA in 30% Danieau solution + 1.5× tricaine) and prewarm to 32°C.
Add 500 μL of the prewarmed 0.3% LMA working solution onto the embryo imaging mold.
Aspirate up to 12 embryos with a glass pipette, allowing them to settle near the bottom of the pipette before dropping into the remaining 500 μL of 0.3% LMA working solution in the tube.
Transfer embryos and remaining solution onto the embryo imaging mold.
Position embryos so that the region of interest is adjacent to the bottom of the imaging cassette for an inverted microscope.
Remove excess 0.3% LMA.
Incubate imaging cassette at 4°C for 5–10 minutes to allow the 0.3% LMA to solidify.
Add 2 mL of 32°C methylcellulose mounting solution on top of the solidified 0.3% LMA.
Incubate embryos at 32°C for 30 minutes prior to imaging.
Recheck orientation before beginning the imaging session and adjust z-stack acquisition settings as necessary.
Obtain z-stacks with a 40×/1.1 W objective over 11–14 hours, maintaining the incubation chamber at 32°C.
